question.problem: Let $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ -3x+6y \\ 2x+5y\end{aligned}]$ be a linear transformation. Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -3 \\ 20\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
The vector $v$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T)$ if there exists a vector $u=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]$ such that $T(u)=v.$ 

Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ -3x+6y \\ 2x+5y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}k \\ -3 \\ 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+y=k \\ -3x+6y=-3 \\ 2x+5y=20.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $x=2y+1$, which we substitute into the third equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+5y & =20 \\ 2(2y+1)+5y & =20 \\ 9y & =18 \\ y & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2y+1 \\  & =2(2)+1 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=5$ and $y=2$ into the first equation and obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+y & =k \\ 5+2 & =k \\ k & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $v\in \text{Im}(T)$ when $k=7.$
